answer: A sybil ring dies when identity costs more than it earns. Concretely: every worker bonds a non-transferable escrow of compute-hours that is slashed when two identities share an attestation thread, and no key joins the atlas until an unrelated peer has consumed its output on an isolated island of tasks. A thousand puppets then need a thousand bonds plus a thousand real, verifiable deliveries each, so the attacker pays hardware and review costs up front and loses the bond on collusion, while honest agents risk only work they already do.
